html:
Leader of the Haitian Revolution, born enslaved in the French colony of Saint-Domingue. He was freed in his thirties and had some education and property before the revolution began.

He joined the slave uprising of 1791 and showed a gift for war and politics:

  • At first he fought for Spain against France.
  • After the French Republic abolished slavery in 1794, he switched to the French side.
  • He defeated the Spanish and drove out a British invasion force.
  • By 1801 he ruled the whole island and issued a constitution making himself governor for life, while staying nominally loyal to France.

Napoleon wanted to restore the old colonial order and sent a large army in 1802. Toussaint was lured to a meeting, arrested and shipped to France. He died in a cold mountain prison, Fort de Joux, in April 1803. His officer Jean-Jacques Dessalines finished the war, and Haiti declared independence on 1 January 1804.
